cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; when applied to a NumericIndicator whose values are [12, 11, 9, 8] the rule is satisfied at index 2 (value 9 crossed under 10) and false at other indexes
cases.description: Verify that crossedUnder(10) creates a CrossedDownIndicatorRule that becomes true when the delegate indicator moves from above 10 to below 10.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [-3, -4, -6, -7] the rule is satisfied at index 2 (value -6 crossed under -5)
cases.description: Check behavior with a negative constant – the rule should trigger when the series drops from >‑5 to ≤‑5.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [1, 0.5, -0.1, -0.5] the rule is satisfied at index 2 (value -0.1 crossed under 0)
cases.description: Edge case where the constant is zero; crossing from positive to negative should satisfy the rule.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [13, 14, 15, 16] the rule is never satisfied because the series never goes from above 15 to below 15
cases.description: Validate that the rule does NOT fire when there is no crossing (values stay below or equal to the constant).
Passing a null Number should result in a NullPointerException (defensive programming).

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [11, 10, 9] the rule is satisfied only at index 2 (value 9) because the previous value (10) is equal to the constant, so the crossing is detected when the series moves from >10 to <=10.
cases.description: Verify that a crossing from exactly the constant to a lower value still triggers the rule (previous > n, current <= n).

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [10, 9] the rule is NOT satisfied at index 1 because the previous value is not greater than the constant (it is equal).
cases.description: Check that a transition from equal to below does NOT count as a crossing when the implementation requires previous > n.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with a single‑element series [12] the rule is never satisfied (no previous value to compare).
cases.description: Edge case: series length of 1 – crossing cannot occur.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with an empty series the rule is never satisfied (no data points).
cases.description: Edge case: empty series – rule should safely return false for all indexes.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [1000000000001, 999999999999] the rule is satisfied at index 1 (value 999999999999) because the series crossed under the large constant.
cases.description: Validate behavior with very large numeric constants.
Passing Double.NaN should be rejected by createConstant and result in an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [1e9, 2e9, 3e9] the rule is never satisfied because a value can never be greater than positive infinity, thus no crossing can occur.
cases.description: Edge case with positive infinity – rule should never fire.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [12, 9, 11, 8, 10, 7] the rule is satisfied at indexes 1, 3 and 5 (values 9, 8, 7) where the series moves from >10 to <=10 multiple times.
cases.description: Verify that the rule correctly identifies multiple crossings in the same series.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedDownIndicatorRule; with delegate values [12, 11, 9] the rule is satisfied at index 2 (value 9) demonstrating that BigDecimal constants are handled correctly.
cases.description: Confirm that createConstant correctly wraps non‑primitive Number types such as BigDecimal.
